# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
#
# gh-1076 (live 2026-10-19, #1074): ONE owner assign spawned THREE runs —
# the `assigned` event plus two `labeled` events from dmtools-factory-
# bot's OWN consequence labels. `types: [assigned, labeled]` fired on
# EVERY label write, so the workflow re-triggered itself on its own
# status:* consequences; gh-1065 dedup made the duplicates self-skip, but
# each still started a run, occupied the concurrency group, spammed the
# run list and cost a probe. GitHub cannot filter label names in `on:`,
# and a job-level `if:` still starts and LISTS the run (the owner's
# explicit complaint) — so the event trigger is `assigned` ONLY.
# Label-driven pickup (arming labels agent:*) continues through the SM
# tick's workflow_dispatch path (gh-1028 dedup), the governed lane.
name: AI Teammate

# gh-1065: the title carries the LEG for every path — the dispatch input
# leg directly, and for event-path runs the strongest arming label on the
# issue (rework > review > pr_approved → review > dev). legOfRunName
# (js/common/teammateEventDedup.js) parses the trailing token, so a
# COMPLETED owner stays title-precise: the strict completed-owner leg rule
# (a leg-less completed run never swallows a KNOWN new leg) can only work
# when real leg runs carry their leg in the title.
# gh-1076: the trailing `|| github.event.label.name` fallback is gone with
# the labeled trigger — labeled events can no longer start this workflow,
# and assigned/dispatch events resolve their leg from the labels above.
# gh-1075: a PR-anchored dispatch ALSO carries the `· pr-<N>` anchor right
# after the issue slot, BEFORE the leg — the gh-1075 fork path always
# backfills inputs.pr, and the SM's pull-keyed leg probe
# (branchLegGuard.hasActiveLegRunForPull) keys on this whole-token anchor
# to suppress a second rework arm on the same fork PR. The anchor sits
# BEFORE the trailing-leg token on purpose: stubTailLegOf (the teammate:
# title family in legOfRunName) parses the leg at the END of the title,
# and the gh-1065 completed-owner leg precision depends on it.
run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format(' · pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) || '' }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && 'rework') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && 'review') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'pr_approved') && 'review') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:dev') && 'dev') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:develop') && 'dev') }}"

on:
  # gh-1076: `assigned` ONLY — see the header. The labeled trigger used to
  # re-fire this workflow on the factory's own consequence labels.
  issues:
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      checkout_ref:
        description: 'gh-1075/gh-1096: refs/pull/<N>/head for fork-PR legs (empty = dispatch ref)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # gh-1065 (live 2026-10-18, issues #1040–#1043 / #1061): one human action
  # (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits MULTIPLE issues events and
  # each event started its own run — two per issue, three on #1061, the
  # owner hand-cancelling duplicates. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM
  # dispatch path only; this job is the missing event-path gate. It probes
  # the repo's ai-teammate.yml runs (per-status gh api fan-out, smAgent
  # parity) and lets the `teammate` call fire only when no OLDER run for
  # the same issue + leg is in flight or freshly completed. Probe errors
  # FAIL OPEN (AC3): a broken check writes proceed=true so the only trigger
  # of a burst is never silently swallowed. The decision itself is the
  # unit-tested pure module js/common/teammateEventDedup.js (AC4) — this
  # step is transport only. The probe short-circuits BEFORE any API call
  # for workflow_dispatch (SM-side gh-1028 governs it) and non-teammate
  # assignees. gh-1076: with the `labeled` trigger removed, the labeled
  # preflight went with it — labeled events can no longer reach this job.
  dedup:
    name: Event-path dedup probe (gh-1065)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # gh-1065 rework (review thread — gh-1029 zero-burn parity): this gate

blocks.text:
# gh-1108: [GOAL] Agents factory publishes per-leg token usage (data/agents-tokens.json) — board TOKENS R/W for all factories

## Description

## Goal — agents factory publishes per-leg token usage (v1, initial card)

One sentence: **the dmtools-agents factory becomes a token-reporting factory** — its factory-data snapshot carries per-leg token usage rows, so the dm.ai board's `TOKENS · R/W` line works for all three factories instead of two.

Today the SM tick's token chain is fully implemented and opt-in (gh-781, gh-825): `factoryState.js` normalizes keyed rows `{leg, at, prompt, completion, total, model, cacheRead}` under `pr-N`/`issue-N`, reads a local tokens file first and falls back to `data/<tokensAsset>.json` on the factory-data branch. flutter_agent_harness publishes and the dm.ai board renders `TOKENS · R 21.4M · W 169k` for it. dmtools-agents publishes state but **no tokens stream at all**: `data/agents-state.json` (factory-data branch, schema 2) carries zero `tokens` keys, there is no `data/agents-tokens.json` (404), and the board renders an honest `TOKENS —` for this factory. The producer half already exists in this repo (`js/aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js`, wired by `ai_teammate_token_usage_reporter.json` → scans completed `ai-teammate.yml` runs, writes `outputs/token_usage/`); what is missing is the **publish path into the tick's reach** (local file in the tick checkout, or the factory-data branch) plus the **asset-name isolation** for a multi-factory branch.

## Why this framing

- Earlier framing considered (extend the board to fetch artifacts directly from workflow runs) is retracted: the board is a static consumer of one JSON per factory; pushing per-run log downloads into the browser duplicates the reporter and breaks the no-rate-limits invariant. The snapshot stays the single transport.
- This card does NOT change the tokens contract — it lands the missing producer→publish→tick link for THIS deployment. Contract owners stay gh-781 (rows) and gh-825 (model/pricing).

## Architecture

```
ai-teammate.yml runs (dmtools-agents)
        │  completed, logs parsed
        ▼
aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter → outputs/token_usage/*.json   [exists]
        │  NEW: keyed rows {leg, at, prompt, completion, total, model, cacheRead}
        │       under 'pr-N' (and 'issue-N' where a leg is issue-anchored)
        ▼
NEW publish step → factory-data branch: data/agents-tokens.json
        │
        ▼
SM tick: statePublish.tokensFile (local) ─miss─▶ fetchTokensFromBranch(repo, cfg)
        │  REQUIRES statePublish.tokensAsset = 'agents-tokens.json'
        ▼
factoryState.buildFactoryState → card.tokens
        ▼
dm.ai /proto/ board → TOKENS · R (prompt+cacheRead) · W (completion)
```

Named invariants:

- **Asset isolation** — `fetchTokensFromBranch` defaults to the fixed asset `fa-tokens.json` (`FACTORY_TOKENS_ASSET`); without `statePublish.tokensAsset: 'agents-tokens.json'` the agents tick would fetch (and silently publish) the WRONG factory's stream on any shared branch. The knob must be set in this deployment's `statePublish` config, and a test must pin that `data/fa-tokens.json` is never consulted by the agents tick.
- **Degradation stays honest** — a tokens miss (file absent, bad shape, revoked scope) must keep publishing token-less cards exactly as today (tokens are decorative, never fatal); provenance stays visible via the tick's 🪙 log line (`local` / `branch:N` / `off — tokens only`).
- **Numbers only** — the published file holds numeric rows and leg/model identifiers. No raw log lines, no prompt text, no URLs beyond what state already publishes. The reporter parses CI logs; its output must byte-scan clean of log excerpts.
- **Schema stays 2** — `card.tokens` is an OPTIONAL additive key (v3 additions ride schema 2 by design); old snapshot readers ignore it.

## Capability surface (everything the reporter allows → our shape)

| Reporter capability | This card | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Parse completed `ai-teammate.yml` runs (perStatusLimit 100, maxLogDownloads 4000) | **core** | existing behavior, unchanged |
| Emit rows keyed `pr-N` for PR legs | **core** | the mapping run→PR the reporter already resolves |
| Emit rows keyed `issue-N` for issue-anchored legs | **second tier** | dev/backlog legs anchor via `#N` in the run summary; if run→issue mapping is unreliable for any leg type, ship pr-N first and file the gap |
| Publish keyed file to `data/agents-tokens.json` on factory-data | **core** | the missing link; same publish shape as fa's gh-781 producer |
| `statePublish.tokensAsset: 'agents-tokens.json'` in the agents SM deployment | **core** | one config line; without it asset isolation breaks |
| `data/model-pricing.json` in the tick checkout (gh-825 $ cost) | **second tier** | optional; absent file = quiet miss, cards render tokens only |
| Backfill beyond perStatusLimit (older runs) | **excluded** | rationale: board is a live view; 24h merged window bounds useful history |
| Streaming/real-time spend, per-message costs | **excluded** | snapshot transport, 10-min cadence is the contract |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — after the producer lands, `data/agents-state.json` cards for PRs with completed ai-teammate runs carry `tokens` rows matching the `normTokenRow` contract (leg, at, prompt, completion, total, model, cacheRead); ≥1 real card observable on the live branch. (E2E + UT)
- **AC2** — with the tokens source absent/invalid, the tick publishes token-less cards and the 🪙 line reads `off — tokens only`; no tick failure, no partial rows. (UT — existing behavior pinned against regression)
- **AC3** — the agents tick never reads `data/fa-tokens.json`: `statePublish.tokensAsset` is set to `agents-tokens.json` and `fetchTokensFromBranch` resolves the agent asset. (UT positive + negative)
- **AC4** — the dm.ai board's HUD shows `TOKENS · R … · W …` when the dmtools-agents factory tab is active, and per-card drawers show Read/Write columns fed by the agents rows. (E2E observation on the live board)
- **AC5** — cacheRead passthrough survives normalization end-to-end (gh-825 rework guard): a producer row with `cache_read` (snake) and one with `cacheRead` (camel) both land on the card. (UT)
- **AC6** — merged_recent cards within the 24h window keep their tokens rows (tmap keys by `pr-N`, merged cards included). (UT)

## Test plan

### Test matrix

- `UT-tok-1..6` → AC1–AC6 in `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` style (pure, no IO): keyed-map shapes, asset-name resolution with/without the knob, degradation paths, snake/camel cacheRead, merged-card tokens carry.
- `UT-prod-1..2` → reporter's keyed emission: a fake runs list maps runs→`pr-N` rows; an unresolvable run yields no row (never a wrong key).
- `IT-pub-1` → publish step writes valid JSON to the branch path with the exact asset name; fixture: one run, one row.
- `E2E-board-1` → live observation: agents factory tab on dm.ai board renders non-dash TOKENS line; AC4.
- **REG guards** — `REG-schema-1`: snapshot asserts `schema === 2` with tokens present (additive-key contract). **CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge even when all other jobs are green.**

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — rows for a PR number that no longer appears in the open/merged lists → silently dropped by the tmap join (honest; no orphan cards).
- **E2** — reporter run for a workflow other than `ai-teammate.yml` → excluded by the existing `workflowId` filter; pinned by UT.
- **E3** — branch fetch races the publish (tokens file momentarily 404) → tick publishes token-less cards this tick; next tick heals. No caching of the failure beyond the tick.
- **E4** — both sources present (local file AND branch) → local wins (existing precedence); pinned.

## Non-goals

- No changes to the tokens row contract, pricing engine, or board rendering code (board side already ships: HUD R/W chip, drawer Read/Write columns — landing repo `src/scripts/boardStats.ts`).
- No backfill of historical runs beyond the reporter's existing window.
- No per-issue cost attribution model beyond the `issue-N` keyed rows.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

blocks.text:
# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine logins ride the
      # deployment-level input (#687, gh-728), exactly like the factory's
      # contract. Comma-separated LIST: the agent harness bot AND the CI
      # bot — github-actions[bot] authors its own PRs (live fa PR #1249)
      # and must ride the machine path (owner directive 2026-10-05).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # App auth (awf#52): minted installation token wins over the PAT
      # inside the factory when both secrets are present.
      APP_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

blocks.text:
# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
#
# gh-1076 (live 2026-10-19, #1074): ONE owner assign spawned THREE runs —
# the `assigned` event plus two `labeled` events from dmtools-factory-
# bot's OWN consequence labels. `types: [assigned, labeled]` fired on
# EVERY label write, so the workflow re-triggered itself on its own
# status:* consequences; gh-1065 dedup made the duplicates self-skip, but
# each still started a run, occupied the concurrency group, spammed the
# run list and cost a probe. GitHub cannot filter label names in `on:`,
# and a job-level `if:` still starts and LISTS the run (the owner's
# explicit complaint) — so the event trigger is `assigned` ONLY.
# Label-driven pickup (arming labels agent:*) continues through the SM
# tick's workflow_dispatch path (gh-1028 dedup), the governed lane.
name: AI Teammate

# gh-1065: the title carries the LEG for every path — the dispatch input
# leg directly, and for event-path runs the strongest arming label on the
# issue (rework > review > pr_approved → review > dev). legOfRunName
# (js/common/teammateEventDedup.js) parses the trailing token, so a
# COMPLETED owner stays title-precise: the strict completed-owner leg rule
# (a leg-less completed run never swallows a KNOWN new leg) can only work
# when real leg runs carry their leg in the title.
# gh-1076: the trailing `|| github.event.label.name` fallback is gone with
# the labeled trigger — labeled events can no longer start this workflow,
# and assigned/dispatch events resolve their leg from the labels above.
# gh-1075: a PR-anchored dispatch ALSO carries the `· pr-<N>` anchor right
# after the issue slot, BEFORE the leg — the gh-1075 fork path always
# backfills inputs.pr, and the SM's pull-keyed leg probe
# (branchLegGuard.hasActiveLegRunForPull) keys on this whole-token anchor
# to suppress a second rework arm on the same fork PR. The anchor sits
# BEFORE the trailing-leg token on purpose: stubTailLegOf (the teammate:
# title family in legOfRunName) parses the leg at the END of the title,
# and the gh-1065 completed-owner leg precision depends on it.
run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format(' · pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) || '' }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && 'rework') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && 'review') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'pr_approved') && 'review') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:dev') && 'dev') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:develop') && 'dev') }}"

on:
  # gh-1076: `assigned` ONLY — see the header. The labeled trigger used to
  # re-fire this workflow on the factory's own consequence labels.
  issues:
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      checkout_ref:
        description: 'gh-1075/gh-1096: refs/pull/<N>/head for fork-PR legs (empty = dispatch ref)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # gh-1065 (live 2026-10-18, issues #1040–#1043 / #1061): one human action
  # (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits MULTIPLE issues events and
  # each event started its own run — two per issue, three on #1061, the
  # owner hand-cancelling duplicates. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM
  # dispatch path only; this job is the missing event-path gate. It probes
  # the repo's ai-teammate.yml runs (per-status gh api fan-out, smAgent
  # parity) and lets the `teammate` call fire only when no OLDER run for
  # the same issue + leg is in flight or freshly completed. Probe errors
  # FAIL OPEN (AC3): a broken check writes proceed=true so the only trigger
  # of a burst is never silently swallowed. The decision itself is the
  # unit-tested pure module js/common/teammateEventDedup.js (AC4) — this
  # step is transport only. The probe short-circuits BEFORE any API call
  # for workflow_dispatch (SM-side gh-1028 governs it) and non-teammate
  # assignees. gh-1076: with the `labeled` trigger removed, the labeled
  # preflight went with it — labeled events can no longer reach this job.
  dedup:
    name: Event-path dedup probe (gh-1065)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # gh-1065 rework (review thread — gh-1029 zero-burn parity): this gate

# gh-1108: [GOAL] Agents factory publishes per-leg token usage (data/agents-tokens.json) — board TOKENS R/W for all factories

## Description

## Goal — agents factory publishes per-leg token usage (v1, initial card)

One sentence: **the dmtools-agents factory becomes a token-reporting factory** — its factory-data snapshot carries per-leg token usage rows, so the dm.ai board's `TOKENS · R/W` line works for all three factories instead of two.

Today the SM tick's token chain is fully implemented and opt-in (gh-781, gh-825): `factoryState.js` normalizes keyed rows `{leg, at, prompt, completion, total, model, cacheRead}` under `pr-N`/`issue-N`, reads a local tokens file first and falls back to `data/<tokensAsset>.json` on the factory-data branch. flutter_agent_harness publishes and the dm.ai board renders `TOKENS · R 21.4M · W 169k` for it. dmtools-agents publishes state but **no tokens stream at all**: `data/agents-state.json` (factory-data branch, schema 2) carries zero `tokens` keys, there is no `data/agents-tokens.json` (404), and the board renders an honest `TOKENS —` for this factory. The producer half already exists in this repo (`js/aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js`, wired by `ai_teammate_token_usage_reporter.json` → scans completed `ai-teammate.yml` runs, writes `outputs/token_usage/`); what is missing is the **publish path into the tick's reach** (local file in the tick checkout, or the factory-data branch) plus the **asset-name isolation** for a multi-factory branch.

## Why this framing

- Earlier framing considered (extend the board to fetch artifacts directly from workflow runs) is retracted: the board is a static consumer of one JSON per factory; pushing per-run log downloads into the browser duplicates the reporter and breaks the no-rate-limits invariant. The snapshot stays the single transport.
- This card does NOT change the tokens contract — it lands the missing producer→publish→tick link for THIS deployment. Contract owners stay gh-781 (rows) and gh-825 (model/pricing).

## Architecture

```
ai-teammate.yml runs (dmtools-agents)
        │  completed, logs parsed
        ▼
aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter → outputs/token_usage/*.json   [exists]
        │  NEW: keyed rows {leg, at, prompt, completion, total, model, cacheRead}
        │       under 'pr-N' (and 'issue-N' where a leg is issue-anchored)
        ▼
NEW publish step → factory-data branch: data/agents-tokens.json
        │
        ▼
SM tick: statePublish.tokensFile (local) ─miss─▶ fetchTokensFromBranch(repo, cfg)
        │  REQUIRES statePublish.tokensAsset = 'agents-tokens.json'
        ▼
factoryState.buildFactoryState → card.tokens
        ▼
dm.ai /proto/ board → TOKENS · R (prompt+cacheRead) · W (completion)
```

Named invariants:

- **Asset isolation** — `fetchTokensFromBranch` defaults to the fixed asset `fa-tokens.json` (`FACTORY_TOKENS_ASSET`); without `statePublish.tokensAsset: 'agents-tokens.json'` the agents tick would fetch (and silently publish) the WRONG factory's stream on any shared branch. The knob must be set in this deployment's `statePublish` config, and a test must pin that `data/fa-tokens.json` is never consulted by the agents tick.
- **Degradation stays honest** — a tokens miss (file absent, bad shape, revoked scope) must keep publishing token-less cards exactly as today (tokens are decorative, never fatal); provenance stays visible via the tick's 🪙 log line (`local` / `branch:N` / `off — tokens only`).
- **Numbers only** — the published file holds numeric rows and leg/model identifiers. No raw log lines, no prompt text, no URLs beyond what state already publishes. The reporter parses CI logs; its output must byte-scan clean of log excerpts.
- **Schema stays 2** — `card.tokens` is an OPTIONAL additive key (v3 additions ride schema 2 by design); old snapshot readers ignore it.

## Capability surface (everything the reporter allows → our shape)

| Reporter capability | This card | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Parse completed `ai-teammate.yml` runs (perStatusLimit 100, maxLogDownloads 4000) | **core** | existing behavior, unchanged |
| Emit rows keyed `pr-N` for PR legs | **core** | the mapping run→PR the reporter already resolves |
| Emit rows keyed `issue-N` for issue-anchored legs | **second tier** | dev/backlog legs anchor via `#N` in the run summary; if run→issue mapping is unreliable for any leg type, ship pr-N first and file the gap |
| Publish keyed file to `data/agents-tokens.json` on factory-data | **core** | the missing link; same publish shape as fa's gh-781 producer |
| `statePublish.tokensAsset: 'agents-tokens.json'` in the agents SM deployment | **core** | one config line; without it asset isolation breaks |
| `data/model-pricing.json` in the tick checkout (gh-825 $ cost) | **second tier** | optional; absent file = quiet miss, cards render tokens only |
| Backfill beyond perStatusLimit (older runs) | **excluded** | rationale: board is a live view; 24h merged window bounds useful history |
| Streaming/real-time spend, per-message costs | **excluded** | snapshot transport, 10-min cadence is the contract |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — after the producer lands, `data/agents-state.json` cards for PRs with completed ai-teammate runs carry `tokens` rows matching the `normTokenRow` contract (leg, at, prompt, completion, total, model, cacheRead); ≥1 real card observable on the live branch. (E2E + UT)
- **AC2** — with the tokens source absent/invalid, the tick publishes token-less cards and the 🪙 line reads `off — tokens only`; no tick failure, no partial rows. (UT — existing behavior pinned against regression)
- **AC3** — the agents tick never reads `data/fa-tokens.json`: `statePublish.tokensAsset` is set to `agents-tokens.json` and `fetchTokensFromBranch` resolves the agent asset. (UT positive + negative)
- **AC4** — the dm.ai board's HUD shows `TOKENS · R … · W …` when the dmtools-agents factory tab is active, and per-card drawers show Read/Write columns fed by the agents rows. (E2E observation on the live board)
- **AC5** — cacheRead passthrough survives normalization end-to-end (gh-825 rework guard): a producer row with `cache_read` (snake) and one with `cacheRead` (camel) both land on the card. (UT)
- **AC6** — merged_recent cards within the 24h window keep their tokens rows (tmap keys by `pr-N`, merged cards included). (UT)

## Test plan

### Test matrix

- `UT-tok-1..6` → AC1–AC6 in `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` style (pure, no IO): keyed-map shapes, asset-name resolution with/without the knob, degradation paths, snake/camel cacheRead, merged-card tokens carry.
- `UT-prod-1..2` → reporter's keyed emission: a fake runs list maps runs→`pr-N` rows; an unresolvable run yields no row (never a wrong key).
- `IT-pub-1` → publish step writes valid JSON to the branch path with the exact asset name; fixture: one run, one row.
- `E2E-board-1` → live observation: agents factory tab on dm.ai board renders non-dash TOKENS line; AC4.
- **REG guards** — `REG-schema-1`: snapshot asserts `schema === 2` with tokens present (additive-key contract). **CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge even when all other jobs are green.**

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — rows for a PR number that no longer appears in the open/merged lists → silently dropped by the tmap join (honest; no orphan cards).
- **E2** — reporter run for a workflow other than `ai-teammate.yml` → excluded by the existing `workflowId` filter; pinned by UT.
- **E3** — branch fetch races the publish (tokens file momentarily 404) → tick publishes token-less cards this tick; next tick heals. No caching of the failure beyond the tick.
- **E4** — both sources present (local file AND branch) → local wins (existing precedence); pinned.

## Non-goals

- No changes to the tokens row contract, pricing engine, or board rendering code (board side already ships: HUD R/W chip, drawer Read/Write columns — landing repo `src/scripts/boardStats.ts`).
- No backfill of historical runs beyond the reporter's existing window.
- No per-issue cost attribution model beyond the `issue-N` keyed rows.
- No dashboard beyond the existing board surface.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine logins ride the
      # deployment-level input (#687, gh-728), exactly like the factory's
      # contract. Comma-separated LIST: the agent harness bot AND the CI
      # bot — github-actions[bot] authors its own PRs (live fa PR #1249)
      # and must ride the machine path (owner directive 2026-10-05).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
#
# gh-1076 (live 2026-10-19, #1074): ONE owner assign spawned THREE runs —
# the `assigned` event plus two `labeled` events from dmtools-factory-
# bot's OWN consequence labels. `types: [assigned, labeled]` fired on
# EVERY label write, so the workflow re-triggered itself on its own
# status:* consequences; gh-1065 dedup made the duplicates self-skip, but
# each still started a run, occupied the concurrency group, spammed the
# run list and cost a probe. GitHub cannot filter label names in `on:`,
# and a job-level `if:` still starts and LISTS the run (the owner's
# explicit complaint) — so the event trigger is `assigned` ONLY.
# Label-driven pickup (arming labels agent:*) continues through the SM
# tick's workflow_dispatch path (gh-1028 dedup), the governed lane.
name: AI Teammate

# gh-1065: the title carries the LEG for every path — the dispatch input
# leg directly, and for event-path runs the strongest arming label on the
# issue (rework > review > pr_approved → review > dev). legOfRunName
# (js/common/teammateEventDedup.js) parses the trailing token, so a
# COMPLETED owner stays title-precise: the strict completed-owner leg rule
# (a leg-less completed run never swallows a KNOWN new leg) can only work
# when real leg runs carry their leg in the title.
# gh-1076: the trailing `|| github.event.label.name` fallback is gone with
# the labeled trigger — labeled events can no longer start this workflow,
# and assigned/dispatch events resolve their leg from the labels above.
# gh-1075: a PR-anchored dispatch ALSO carries the `· pr-<N>` anchor right
# after the issue slot, BEFORE the leg — the gh-1075 fork path always
# backfills inputs.pr, and the SM's pull-keyed leg probe
# (branchLegGuard.hasActiveLegRunForPull) keys on this whole-token anchor
# to suppress a second rework arm on the same fork PR. The anchor sits
# BEFORE the trailing-leg token on purpose: stubTailLegOf (the teammate:
# title family in legOfRunName) parses the leg at the END of the title,
# and the gh-1065 completed-owner leg precision depends on it.
run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format(' · pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) || '' }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && 'rework') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && 'review') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'pr_approved') && 'review') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:dev') && 'dev') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:develop') && 'dev') }}"

on:
  # gh-1076: `assigned` ONLY — see the header. The labeled trigger used to
  # re-fire this workflow on the factory's own consequence labels.
  issues:
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      checkout_ref:
        description: 'gh-1075/gh-1096: refs/pull/<N>/head for fork-PR legs (empty = dispatch ref)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # gh-1065 (live 2026-10-18, issues #1040–#1043 / #1061): one human action
  # (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits MULTIPLE issues events and
  # each event started its own run — two per issue, three on #1061, the
  # owner hand-cancelling duplicates. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM
  # dispatch path only; this job is the missing event-path gate. It probes
  # the repo's ai-teammate.yml runs (per-status gh api fan-out, smAgent
  # parity) and lets the `teammate` call fire only when no OLDER run for
  # the same issue + leg is in flight or freshly completed. Probe errors
  # FAIL OPEN (AC3): a broken check writes proceed=true so the only trigger
  # of a burst is never silently swallowed. The decision itself is the
  # unit-tested pure module js/common/teammateEventDedup.js (AC4) — this
  # step is transport only. The probe short-circuits BEFORE any API call
  # for workflow_dispatch (SM-side gh-1028 governs it) and non-teammate
  # assignees. gh-1076: with the `labeled` trigger removed, the labeled
  # preflight went with it — labeled events can no longer reach this job.
  dedup:
    name: Event-path dedup probe (gh-1065)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # gh-1065 rework (review thread — gh-1029 zero-burn parity): this gate

# gh-1108: [GOAL] Agents factory publishes per-leg token usage (data/agents-tokens.json) — board TOKENS R/W for all factories

## Description

## Goal — agents factory publishes per-leg token usage (v1, initial card)

One sentence: **the dmtools-agents factory becomes a token-reporting factory** — its factory-data snapshot carries per-leg token usage rows, so the dm.ai board's `TOKENS · R/W` line works for all three factories instead of two.

Today the SM tick's token chain is fully implemented and opt-in (gh-781, gh-825): `factoryState.js` normalizes keyed rows `{leg, at, prompt, completion, total, model, cacheRead}` under `pr-N`/`issue-N`, reads a local tokens file first and falls back to `data/<tokensAsset>.json` on the factory-data branch. flutter_agent_harness publishes and the dm.ai board renders `TOKENS · R 21.4M · W 169k` for it. dmtools-agents publishes state but **no tokens stream at all**: `data/agents-state.json` (factory-data branch, schema 2) carries zero `tokens` keys, there is no `data/agents-tokens.json` (404), and the board renders an honest `TOKENS —` for this factory. The producer half already exists in this repo (`js/aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js`, wired by `ai_teammate_token_usage_reporter.json` → scans completed `ai-teammate.yml` runs, writes `outputs/token_usage/`); what is missing is the **publish path into the tick's reach** (local file in the tick checkout, or the factory-data branch) plus the **asset-name isolation** for a multi-factory branch.

## Why this framing

- Earlier framing considered (extend the board to fetch artifacts directly from workflow runs) is retracted: the board is a static consumer of one JSON per factory; pushing per-run log downloads into the browser duplicates the reporter and breaks the no-rate-limits invariant. The snapshot stays the single transport.
- This card does NOT change the tokens contract — it lands the missing producer→publish→tick link for THIS deployment. Contract owners stay gh-781 (rows) and gh-825 (model/pricing).

## Architecture

```
ai-teammate.yml runs (dmtools-agents)
        │  completed, logs parsed
        ▼
aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter → outputs/token_usage/*.json   [exists]
        │  NEW: keyed rows {leg, at, prompt, completion, total, model, cacheRead}
        │       under 'pr-N' (and 'issue-N' where a leg is issue-anchored)
        ▼
NEW publish step → factory-data branch: data/agents-tokens.json
        │
        ▼
SM tick: statePublish.tokensFile (local) ─miss─▶ fetchTokensFromBranch(repo, cfg)
        │  REQUIRES statePublish.tokensAsset = 'agents-tokens.json'
        ▼
factoryState.buildFactoryState → card.tokens
        ▼
dm.ai /proto/ board → TOKENS · R (prompt+cacheRead) · W (completion)
```

Named invariants:

- **Asset isolation** — `fetchTokensFromBranch` defaults to the fixed asset `fa-tokens.json` (`FACTORY_TOKENS_ASSET`); without `statePublish.tokensAsset: 'agents-tokens.json'` the agents tick would fetch (and silently publish) the WRONG factory's stream on any shared branch. The knob must be set in this deployment's `statePublish` config, and a test must pin that `data/fa-tokens.json` is never consulted by the agents tick.
- **Degradation stays honest** — a tokens miss (file absent, bad shape, revoked scope) must keep publishing token-less cards exactly as today (tokens are decorative, never fatal); provenance stays visible via the tick's 🪙 log line (`local` / `branch:N` / `off — tokens only`).
- **Numbers only** — the published file holds numeric rows and leg/model identifiers. No raw log lines, no prompt text, no URLs beyond what state already publishes. The reporter parses CI logs; its output must byte-scan clean of log excerpts.
- **Schema stays 2** — `card.tokens` is an OPTIONAL additive key (v3 additions ride schema 2 by design); old snapshot readers ignore it.

## Capability surface (everything the reporter allows → our shape)

| Reporter capability | This card | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Parse completed `ai-teammate.yml` runs (perStatusLimit 100, maxLogDownloads 4000) | **core** | existing behavior, unchanged |
| Emit rows keyed `pr-N` for PR legs | **core** | the mapping run→PR the reporter already resolves |
| Emit rows keyed `issue-N` for issue-anchored legs | **second tier** | dev/backlog legs anchor via `#N` in the run summary; if run→issue mapping is unreliable for any leg type, ship pr-N first and file the gap |
| Publish keyed file to `data/agents-tokens.json` on factory-data | **core** | the missing link; same publish shape as fa's gh-781 producer |
| `statePublish.tokensAsset: 'agents-tokens.json'` in the agents SM deployment | **core** | one config line; without it asset isolation breaks |
| `data/model-pricing.json` in the tick checkout (gh-825 $ cost) | **second tier** | optional; absent file = quiet miss, cards render tokens only |
| Backfill beyond perStatusLimit (older runs) | **excluded** | rationale: board is a live view; 24h merged window bounds useful history |
| Streaming/real-time spend, per-message costs | **excluded** | snapshot transport, 10-min cadence is the contract |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — after the producer lands, `data/agents-state.json` cards for PRs with completed ai-teammate runs carry `tokens` rows matching the `normTokenRow` contract (leg, at, prompt, completion, total, model, cacheRead); ≥1 real card observable on the live branch. (E2E + UT)
- **AC2** — with the tokens source absent/invalid, the tick publishes token-less cards and the 🪙 line reads `off — tokens only`; no tick failure, no partial rows. (UT — existing behavior pinned against regression)
- **AC3** — the agents tick never reads `data/fa-tokens.json`: `statePublish.tokensAsset` is set to `agents-tokens.json` and `fetchTokensFromBranch` resolves the agent asset. (UT positive + negative)
- **AC4** — the dm.ai board's HUD shows `TOKENS · R … · W …` when the dmtools-agents factory tab is active, and per-card drawers show Read/Write columns fed by the agents rows. (E2E observation on the live board)
- **AC5** — cacheRead passthrough survives normalization end-to-end (gh-825 rework guard): a producer row with `cache_read` (snake) and one with `cacheRead` (camel) both land on the card. (UT)
- **AC6** — merged_recent cards within the 24h window keep their tokens rows (tmap keys by `pr-N`, merged cards included). (UT)

## Test plan

### Test matrix

- `UT-tok-1..6` → AC1–AC6 in `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` style (pure, no IO): keyed-map shapes, asset-name resolution with/without the knob, degradation paths, snake/camel cacheRead, merged-card tokens carry.
- `UT-prod-1..2` → reporter's keyed emission: a fake runs list maps runs→`pr-N` rows; an unresolvable run yields no row (never a wrong key).
- `IT-pub-1` → publish step writes valid JSON to the branch path with the exact asset name; fixture: one run, one row.
- `E2E-board-1` → live observation: agents factory tab on dm.ai board renders non-dash TOKENS line; AC4.
- **REG guards** — `REG-schema-1`: snapshot asserts `schema === 2` with tokens present (additive-key contract). **CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge even when all other jobs are green.**

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — rows for a PR number that no longer appears in the open/merged lists → silently dropped by the tmap join (honest; no orphan cards).
- **E2** — reporter run for a workflow other than `ai-teammate.yml` → excluded by the existing `workflowId` filter; pinned by UT.
- **E3** — branch fetch races the publish (tokens file momentarily 404) → tick publishes token-less cards this tick; next tick heals. No caching of the failure beyond the tick.
- **E4** — both sources present (local file AND branch) → local wins (existing precedence); pinned.

## Non-goals

- No changes to the tokens row contract, pricing engine, or board rendering code (board side already ships: HUD R/W chip, drawer Read/Write columns — landing repo `src/scripts/boardStats.ts`).
- No backfill of historical runs beyond the reporter's existing window.
- No per-issue cost attribution model beyond the `issue-N` keyed rows.
- No dashboard beyond the existing board surface.

## Open questions

1. **Publish path owner** — exten…

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

blocks.text:
# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine logins ride the
      # deployment-level input (#687, gh-728), exactly like the factory's
      # contract. Comma-separated LIST: the agent harness bot AND the CI
      # bot — github-actions[bot] authors its own PRs (live fa PR #1249)
      # and must ride the machine path (owner directive 2026-10-05).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # App auth (awf#52): minted installation token wins over the PAT
      # inside the factory when both secrets are present.
      APP_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}
